name: Metabolic disease due to other fatty acid oxidation disorder

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Fatty Acid Oxidation Disorder Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Episodes of hypoketotic hypoglycemia or metabolic acidosis triggered by fasting or illness
Elevated plasma acylcarnitine profile consistent with fatty acid oxidation defect
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes encoding fatty acid oxidation enzymes
Reduced activity of specific mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation enzymes in fibroblasts or lymphocytes
Histological evidence of lipid accumulation in muscle tissue

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical presentation plus abnormal biochemical markers and/or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may require combination of clinical, biochemical, and genetic data due to phenotypic variability.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic low ketone levels despite hypoglycemia during metabolic crises

pathognomonic.symptomName: Metabolic acidosis during fasting or illness
pathognomonic.notes: Severe acid-base imbalance triggered by catabolic stress
searchTerms: acid buildup in blood during fasting
low blood pH in metabolic crisis

common.notes: Dilated or hypertrophic forms reported in some patients
Liver enlargement due to fat accumulation

occasional.notes: Muscle breakdown with myoglobinuria during metabolic stress
Sensory and motor deficits in some cases
Irregular heart rhythms possibly related to cardiomyopathy

searchTerms: failure to gain weight as baby

rare.notes: Rare visual impairment due to retinal changes

laboratory: Elevated plasma acylcarnitines (specific chain lengths depending on enzyme defect)
Metabolic acidosis with elevated anion gap
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes encoding mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation enzymes (e.g., ACADVL, CPT2, HADHA)
other: Reduced enzyme activity in fibroblast or lymphocyte assays

distinguishingFeatures: More common fatty acid oxidation disorder
Typically presents in infancy with hypoglycemia
Different genetic etiology affecting glycogen metabolism

redFlags: Recurrent hypoketotic hypoglycemia with metabolic acidosis
Sudden cardiac arrest or arrhythmia in young patient
Severe rhabdomyolysis triggered by fasting or illness
references: Roe CR, et al. Fatty acid oxidation disorders. In: Scriver CR, et al., editors. The Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease. 8th ed. McGraw-Hill; 2001.
Spiekerkoetter U, et al. Fatty acid oxidation disorders: diagnosis and management. J Inherit Metab Dis. 2010;33(5): 527-535.
